title: Twin-cell glass-panel DRAM with invalid-pair erasure decoding
idea: Box [medium: capacitor charge | access: LTPS planar TFT | sense: differential twin-cell | integration: chiplet | substrate: Gen-6 glass panel | fab: i-line/DUV panel litho]. Each bit is a complementary cell pair on cheap panel-made arrays; a pair that senses 00 or 11 (one cell leaked or dead) is flagged as an erasure, and a Reed-Solomon code over 32-pair symbols corrects ~2x more erasures than unknown errors.
why: Fact 4 capital: lets panel fabs with ~1e-3 raw cell failure ship usable working memory; ~2x cell area but ~10x lower capex per m2 of array.

title: Deliberately weakened sentinel cell per row triggers refresh
idea: Box [medium: capacitor + 60%-size sentinel capacitor | access: planar | sense: sentinel comparator at high reference | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk Si | fab: DUV]. Each row carries one intentionally weak sentinel written '1' at every refresh; every activation and a low-energy idle sweep of only the sentinel column check it, and a decayed sentinel triggers that row's refresh, so each row is refreshed on its own physical clock.
why: Fact 3 retention tail: replaces worst-case 32/64 ms refresh with per-row physical timing; ~3-5x fewer refreshes, recovering much of the 10-20% bandwidth loss.

title: Per-row-pair SOI back-gate pulses block row hammer injection
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: thin-body FD-SOI transistor | sense: standard | integration: monolithic | substrate: SOI with patterned back-gate strips | fab: DUV]. A back-gate strip runs under every row pair; when row N opens, the controller drives the neighbours' strips to about -1.5 V for the open time, raising their Vt and repelling electrons that migrate from the aggressor channel into victim storage nodes.
why: Fact 9: targets the electron-migration mechanism behind ~1k-activation flips; aims for >20x higher hammer threshold without refresh-based mitigation.

title: Ferroelectric remnant in capacitor gives LDPC a second opinion
idea: Box [medium: Hf/Zr-oxide capacitor with a tuned small ferroelectric remnant | access: standard | sense: dual-mode charge + polarization | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: ALD]. The bit is stored as charge, but each write also nudges a weak, slowly relaxing polarization; when ECC fails, a second polarization read supplies a likelihood value per bit so LDPC soft decoding recovers words that hard decoding cannot.
why: Facts 1/3: a free, physically independent second copy lets smaller-Cs or leakier cells pass; ~10x lower uncorrectable rate at equal raw BER.

title: Discharge-slope telemetry from normal reads builds live retention map
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: time-to-digital sense amp | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: EUV]. Each sense amp records the picoseconds the bitline takes to cross a threshold, which encodes the cell's remaining charge; the controller turns these free samples from ordinary reads into a continuously updated per-row retention class and adapts each row's refresh period.
why: Fact 3: retention profiling with no test downtime that also catches variable-retention-time cells live; ~4x fewer refresh operations.

title: Co-aged reference cells cancel drift in printed ionic memory
idea: Box [medium: proton-intercalation WO3 ionic cell | access: printed organic diode | sense: ratiometric current | integration: 3D printed tiers | substrate: polymer foil | fab: inkjet printing]. Every row write also writes four reference cells to known levels at the same instant so they age identically; reads compare each data cell against interpolated co-aged references, cancelling time and temperature drift.
why: Capital and scarce resources: makes very cheap, drift-prone printed media usable as working memory; drift-induced errors suppressed ~100x.

title: Bit-significance routing across strong and derated memory pools
idea: Box [medium: recycled or derated DRAM dies | access: standard | sense: standard | integration: CXL memory pool | substrate: reclaimed DIMMs | fab: legacy]. A CXL controller bit-slices bf16/fp8 tensors so sign and exponent bits land in a chipkill-protected pool while low mantissa bits land in end-of-life or out-of-spec dies with no ECC and 4x relaxed refresh.
why: Supply: returns retired and downbinned DRAM to service; ~30-50% of AI memory capacity can tolerate flips with <1% accuracy impact.

title: Split buried wordline turns passing gate into negative shield
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: buried-channel transistor | sense: standard | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: EUV + split-gate etch]. The buried wordline is split so the segment that passes beside a neighbour's storage junction becomes a separately biased shield held at about -0.4 V, so toggling the aggressor no longer gates the victim's junction (the passing-gate hammer path).
why: Fact 9: removes the dominant passing-wordline hammer mechanism physically; ~10x higher hammer threshold claimed with no refresh overhead.

title: Electro-optic imaging maps every cell's retention at wafer sort
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: standard | sense: optical, via removable electro-optic polymer film | integration: wafer-level test | substrate: bulk | fab: temporary spin-on film]. At sort a removable Pockels-effect film over the array is imaged with polarized light while cells decay, capturing every cell's leakage curve in seconds; the per-die map is fused on chip to drive repair and per-row refresh classes.
why: Facts 3/4: replaces hours of electrical retention testing with seconds of imaging and enables shipping weak dies with exact maps; ~5% more sellable dies.

title: ReRAM CAM repairs individual failing bits in the field
idea: Box [medium: capacitor + side ReRAM CAM | access: standard | sense: standard + CAM match | integration: monolithic BEOL | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. A 64k-entry ReRAM content-addressable table in the periphery stores failing-cell addresses found by boot-time BIST and supplies the replacement bit on a match, dropping repair granularity from whole rows or columns to single bits.
why: Yield and Fact 3: dies with ~1e-5 scattered weak cells ship and tail cells are repaired instead of driving refresh; ~5-10% die-yield recovery.

title: Run legacy-node U.S. DRAM at 77 K to erase tails
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar at 77 K | sense: standard | integration: liquid-nitrogen-cooled memory sled | substrate: bulk | fab: 25-30 nm DUV legacy process]. Junction and GIDL leakage fall >1000x at 77 K, so retention moves from 64 ms to minutes and weak tail cells become strong; older, EUV-free nodes with bigger, cheaper cells then serve disaggregated LN2-cooled memory racks.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: no EUV, refresh (16-33% of idle power) nearly disappears; cooling overhead offsets about half of the energy gain.

title: HBM stack RAID with a parity die and live rebuild
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: standard | sense: standard | integration: 12-high HBM stack | substrate: bulk | fab: standard]. One die of a 12-high stack holds XOR/RS parity across the other 11, so a die with dead TSVs, a failed bank or a hammer-corrupted row is reconstructed on the fly instead of scrapping the whole stack.
why: Fact 6: converts 20-30% stack yield loss into ~8% capacity overhead and ships stacks that fail today.

title: On-die microheater anneals re-passivate leakage traps in the field
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: standard | integration: monolithic with polysilicon heater meander under each bank | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Every few months the controller migrates one bank's data to a neighbour, heats the bank to ~250 C for ~100 ms, and lets hydrogen re-passivate the interface traps that create GIDL and variable-retention tails.
why: Fact 3: restores aged retention tails and slows refresh-rate growth over device life; ~2x tail improvement claimed.

title: Analog leaky integrator capacitor counts hammers per row
idea: Box [medium: per-row MOS integrator capacitor | access: charge-packet injection on each ACT | sense: threshold comparator | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Every activation dumps a fixed charge packet onto a tiny per-row integrator that leaks with a time constant matched to the refresh window; crossing threshold triggers neighbour refresh, giving an exact per-row counter for about one cell's area.
why: Fact 9: deterministic tracking at hammer thresholds of 1k and below with <1% area, versus 5-10% for SRAM counter tables.

title: Relaxed DUV array bonded to logic doing per-mat BCH
idea: Box [medium: capacitor at relaxed 18 nm | access: vertical channel | sense: on bonded logic wafer | integration: wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV-only array + advanced logic]. The array wafer skips EUV and accepts ~1e-4 raw BER, while the bonded logic wafer runs a t=8 BCH decoder beside every 512-bit mat word through ~1 um pitch bonds.
why: Facts 4/7: removes 5-7 EUV layers from the array and moves periphery off the array die; ~30% lower cost per bit.

title: Sixteen-subcell majority bits from nanoimprinted crossbars
idea: Box [medium: 16 nano-capacitors per bit | access: crossbar diode | sense: ensemble charge summing | integration: monolithic | substrate: glass | fab: nanoimprint lithography]. Each bit is a cluster of 16 sub-10 nm imprinted capacitors on one local bitline sensed as a summed charge, so up to ~5 dead or leaky subcells per bit change nothing.
why: Facts 1/4: swaps defect-free EUV patterning for defect-tolerant imprint; ~5x lower patterning cost per layer.

title: Self-clearing capacitor electrode isolates dielectric leakage hot spots
idea: Box [medium: capacitor with MnOx/VO2-type top electrode | access: standard | sense: standard | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: ALD]. The top electrode is a conductive oxide that converts to an insulating phase where local leakage current heats it (as MnO2 does in tantalum capacitors), so a weak dielectric spot clears itself during a forming pulse instead of becoming a retention-tail cell.
why: Facts 1/3: allows thinner, higher-k, more defective dielectrics (more Cs at lower aspect ratio) by healing defects; ~10x tail shift claimed.

title: Grade-B DRAM exchange selling dies with certified error maps
idea: Box [medium: any | access: any | sense: standard | integration: DIMM or CXL | substrate: bulk | fab: existing fabs]. A broker buys dies that fail JEDEC retention or hammer limits, tests each to a signed per-die error map, and sells them to hyperscalers whose controllers load the map to retire rows and set per-bank refresh.
why: Supply: unlocks the 5-15% of output that is scrapped or downbinned today, at ~40% discount.

title: JEDEC relaxed-retention DRAM grade with mandatory host chipkill
idea: Box [policy layer over medium: capacitor | access: standard | sense: standard | integration: DIMM | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. Standardize a DRAM grade with 16 ms base retention, readable per-bank retention-class registers and mandatory host chipkill, so fabs can ship dies that fail the 64 ms spec as standard parts.
why: Supply and yield: +5-10% usable output per wafer and a faster yield ramp for new U.S. fabs.

title: Layer recompute replaces ECC for AI training activations
idea: Box [medium: ECC-free cheap DRAM | access: standard | sense: 32-bit CRC per tile | integration: accelerator HBM | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. Activations saved for the backward pass go into ECC-less, relaxed-refresh memory with a CRC per tile; a mismatch triggers recomputation of that layer from the last checkpoint, which costs <1% compute at observed error rates.
why: Reliability tax: drops 12.5% ECC overhead and lets ~2x weaker memory hold 40-60% of the training footprint.

title: Bistable NEMS beam tier quarantines hammer-hot rows
idea: Box [medium: bistable buckled nanobeam | access: electrostatic actuation | sense: capacitive position | integration: BEOL MEMS above array | substrate: bulk | fab: sacrificial-release MEMS]. A small on-die tier of mechanically latched cells, which hold no disturbable charge and do not leak, receives rows the controller flags as hammered or leaky until they cool.
why: Facts 9/3: physically immune cells absorb the worst ~0.1% of rows, removing most mitigation refreshes.

title: Carbon-doped gettering liner between rows traps migrating electrons
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: vertical channel | sense: standard | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk with carbon-implanted isolation liner | fab: DUV implant]. The isolation between adjacent rows is lined with carbon-doped silicon that creates recombination centres >50 nm from storage junctions, so electrons injected by a toggling aggressor recombine before reaching the victim node.
why: Fact 9: raises hammer threshold ~5-10x passively; the risk is adding retention tail, controlled by keeping the liner away from junctions.

title: Refresh-time 2D parity scrubbing computed inside sense amplifiers
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: standard | sense: sense amps with XOR accumulator latch | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. During each refresh sweep the sense amps XOR every refreshed row into a column-parity latch and compare it with a stored parity row (updated by write deltas), while per-row parity bits flag the row, so the row-column intersection locates and fixes single flips at zero extra activations.
why: Facts 3/9: turns refresh into scrubbing that catches retention and hammer flips before they accumulate, with no extra bandwidth.

title: Speculative 0.3 V bitline read with ECC-triggered escalation
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: low-swing latch + slow offset-cancelled backup amp | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. The array runs at VARY 0.3 V with ~30 mV sense margin; on-die ECC checks every read and only failing codewords (~0.1%) are re-sensed by a slow, offset-cancelled high-gain amplifier and rewritten at 0.6 V.
why: Constraint/Fact 10: bitline CV^2 falls ~11x and escalations add <2%; reliability comes from detect-and-retry, not static margin.

title: Segment-aligned ECC codewords enable 64-bit micro-activations
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: segmented local wordline | sense: local sense per 72-cell segment | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Only one 64+8-bit segment of a row is raised and the whole ECC codeword lives inside that segment, so small accesses keep full SECDED protection and hammer disturbance and counters are confined to segment neighbours.
why: Constraint/Fact 8: removes the ~128x page overfetch, ~10-30x lower activation energy per useful bit, and shrinks hammer exposure per access.

title: Bonded local sense amps per 32 cells rescue tiny capacitors
idea: Box [medium: 1 fF capacitor | access: vertical channel | sense: one sense amp per 32-cell bitline on a bonded logic wafer | integration: hybrid bonding at 0.5 um pitch | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Bitline capacitance drops ~16x, so a 1 fF cell gives more signal than a 5 fF cell does today while each sense event only charges a tiny bitline.
why: Constraint: ~10x lower bitline energy per access; Fact 1: capacitor aspect ratio can fall from ~70:1 to ~15:1, and weak cells gain margin.

title: Resonant adiabatic wordline drivers recycle charge and soften hammer edges
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: standard | integration: monolithic + in-package LC tank inductor | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Wordlines are swung by a shared resonant LC tank with a ~2 ns sinusoidal ramp, returning most wordline charge to the tank instead of dumping it, and the slower dV/dt cuts capacitive coupling and electron injection into neighbour rows.
why: Constraint: wordline plus ~30%-efficient VPP-pump energy falls ~5-10x; Fact 9: smoother edges raise the hammer threshold modestly.

title: Z-channel coding lets a one be stored at eighth charge
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: asymmetric reference near the empty level | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Because DRAM charge only leaks away (1->0), the sense reference sits just above empty with a small guard band and '1' is written at ~0.35 V; the rare 1->0 losses are fixed by a unidirectional Bose-Lin code needing ~half the check bits of symmetric BCH.
why: Constraint: write/restore charge and bitline swing fall ~8-10x; the code matches the physics of the error channel.

title: Per-row ferroelectric Vt trim of access transistors lowers wordline swing
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: FeFET access transistor with HZO gate layer | sense: standard | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: ALD]. At test and periodically in the field, each row's access-transistor Vt is trimmed by partially polarizing its ferroelectric gate, pulling leaky-tail rows up and slow rows down, so the wordline can swing ~1.3 V instead of ~3 V without a leakage tail.
why: Constraint: wordline CV^2 ~5x lower and the VPP pump removed, ~10x on the wordline path; Fact 3: leakage tail compressed by trimming.

title: Corrected-error-rate feedback drives each bank to its own Vmin
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: standard with per-bank VARY/VPP regulators | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. An on-die loop lowers each bank's VARY and VPP in 10 mV steps until the ECC-corrected error rate hits a target such as 1 per 1e9 bits, and raises them on temperature rise or error bursts, removing worst-silicon, worst-temperature and end-of-life guard bands.
why: Constraint: typical banks settle near 0.4-0.5 V versus the 1 V spec (~4-6x CV^2), and VPP scaling brings the wordline path to ~8-10x; reliability is a measured, regulated quantity.

title: Sub-critical stochastic MTJ writes with ECC absorbing misses
idea: Box [medium: perpendicular MTJ | access: spin-orbit-torque line | sense: TMR at 50 mV bias | integration: BEOL over CMOS | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Writes use a short pulse at ~60% of deterministic switching current so ~1e-3 of bits fail to switch; instead of write-verify loops, a BCH code over each 512-bit word absorbs them and background scrubbing rewrites only failed bits.
why: Constraint: write energy ~5-10x lower and low-bias reads keep read energy small; byte-addressable nonvolatile cell with no refresh.

title: Capacitively bootstrapped neighbor wordlines dip negative during activation
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: low-Vt planar | sense: standard | integration: monolithic with MIM coupling caps between adjacent wordline drivers | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. A small coupling capacitor between each wordline driver and its neighbours' hold nodes pulls neighbours ~0.5 V negative exactly while the aggressor is high, passively closing victim access devices; this lets a low-Vt access transistor run with a ~1.5 V wordline.
why: Constraint: no counter or mitigation-refresh energy (which grows toward several times access energy at hammer thresholds near 100), plus ~4x lower wordline CV^2, ~10x on the activation path.

title: Non-switching butterfly-capacitance read of ferroelectric cells
idea: Box [medium: HZO ferroelectric capacitor | access: planar | sense: small-signal capacitance at a fixed plate bias | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: ALD]. Instead of switching polarization to read it, the sense circuit applies a 50 mV probe at a fixed bias and measures differential capacitance, which differs between the two polarization branches of the butterfly C-V curve; the weak signal is decoded with soft ECC.
why: Constraint: no 2Pr switching charge moves on reads, ~10-30x lower read energy; reliability: removes read fatigue and wake-up wear, so endurance becomes effectively unlimited.

title: Minutes-retention trap-charge cell with age-stamped scrubbing
idea: Box [medium: charge in SiN trap layer behind ~1.5 nm tunnel oxide | access: 1T gate-coupled storage | sense: Vt current sense | integration: 3D vertical stack | substrate: bulk | fab: NAND-style tools, no EUV]. Bits are written by low-voltage direct tunneling in nanoseconds and retained for minutes; reads sense transistor Vt without disturbing charge, and each block carries an age stamp so only blocks nearing their retention budget are scrubbed.
why: Constraint: a read is a small current pulse on a short line with no restore, ~10x below ACT+restore; refresh ~1000x rarer.

title: Compress-then-protect: freed bits buy strong ECC at 0.4 V
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: low-swing | integration: codec on HBM/CXL logic base die | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. Each 64 B line is compressed (base-delta or zero-run) to at most 40 B, and the freed 24 B hold strong BCH/LDPC parity so that region runs at 0.4 V; incompressible lines (~25%) go to a 1 V region.
why: Constraint: ~1.6x fewer bits moved times ~6x lower array CV^2 gives ~10x per useful bit; parity costs no capacity.

title: On-die segment cache absorbs repeat activations and caps hammering
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: standard | integration: 256 KB SRAM segment cache per bank group | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Recently activated 64 B segments stay in an SRAM cache beside the bank; repeat accesses hit SRAM instead of re-activating, and any row that hits the cache N times is pinned there so it can never be hammered past N.
why: Constraint: for AI/KV workloads with >80% segment reuse, average access energy ~5-10x lower; Fact 9 bounded by construction.

title: Golden-copy flash backing replaces ECC and refresh for weights
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: low-swing | integration: DRAM + NAND in one package | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. Immutable inference weights live in a 0.4 V, ECC-less, refresh-relaxed DRAM region with a 16-bit CRC per 256 B; a CRC failure refetches that line from the packaged NAND golden copy and rewrites it.
why: Constraint: ~6x lower CV^2 plus near-zero refresh gives ~10x amortized energy per access; reliability comes from the backing store, not margin.

title: Redundant-residue in-DRAM arithmetic self-corrects low-voltage compute errors
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: bit-serial compute sense amps | integration: processing-in-memory subarrays | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Values are stored as residues modulo small coprime moduli plus two redundant moduli; sense-amp adders do multiply-accumulate in each residue channel independently at 0.4 V, and the redundant residues locate and correct a faulty channel.
why: Constraint/Fact 5: data never leaves the subarray, ~10-20x less energy than moving it to an accelerator; residues confine errors so low-voltage compute stays exact.

title: Hundred-electron storage nodes read by single-electron electrometers
idea: Box [medium: ~100-electron Si quantum-dot node | access: Si nanowire gate | sense: single-electron transistor electrometer | integration: monolithic | substrate: SOI | fab: e-beam or DSA]. Each bit is ~100 electrons sensed by a capacitively coupled SET that resolves single electrons, stored as 3-way repetition with Poisson-aware soft decoding that treats leakage as counting noise.
why: Constraint: stored charge ~16 aC versus ~5 fC, so access energy can fall >100x; Fact 1: removes the capacitor entirely.

title: One end-to-end codeword spans array, link and controller
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: low-margin | integration: DIMM or CXL with host-side decoder | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. The host encodes once with a strong LDPC and the DRAM stores and returns the raw codeword with no on-die ECC or link CRC, so one parity budget absorbs both ~1e-4 errors from a 0.45 V array and errors from a ~100 mV-swing link.
why: Constraint/Fact 5: I/O energy (dominant in DDR5's 10-20 pJ/bit) and array CV^2 both drop ~4-5x, ~10x combined, and on-die ECC logic disappears.

title: Energy-grade DRAM bins sold against a contracted raw BER
idea: Box [medium: any | access: standard | sense: standard | integration: hyperscaler-owned host decoder | substrate: bulk | fab: existing fabs]. Fabs test each die for the lowest VARY/VPP that meets a contracted raw BER (e.g., 1e-5) instead of zero errors and sell it as an 'E-grade' part priced per pJ/access to buyers who run strong host codes.
why: Constraint: many dies reach 0.45-0.5 V at 1e-5 BER, ~5-10x lower CV^2 per access; monetizes margin that zero-error specs throw away.

title: JEDEC soft-information pins export per-read confidence to hosts
idea: Box [medium: any | access: standard | sense: sense amp with margin comparator | integration: standard DIMM | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. A JEDEC standard adds one confidence bit per 8 data bits, set when the sense differential fell below a guard threshold, so host decoders treat low-confidence bits as erasures and arrays can run at much lower voltage.
why: Constraint: erasure decoding roughly doubles correctable errors at equal parity, letting VARY drop ~2.5x (~6-10x CV^2); a policy that unlocks it industry-wide.

title: Pair-encoded ternary weights where every decay lands on zero
idea: Box [medium: capacitor pair per trit | access: planar | sense: dual-cell ternary sense | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Pruned AI weights are stored as +1 = cell A charged, -1 = cell B charged, 0 = both empty, so zero weights move no charge and every leakage event decays a weight toward 0 rather than flipping its sign.
why: Constraint: at 80-90% sparsity most cells move no charge on access or restore, ~5-10x lower energy; reliability: the only possible error direction is benign shrinkage.

title: Wavelength-addressed optical wordlines open single row segments
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: Ge photo-FET | sense: standard | integration: SiN waveguide wordlines with ring filters | substrate: SOI | fab: DUV]. Each row is opened by light: a waveguide over the row carries several wavelengths and ring filters steer each wavelength to one 64-bit segment of photo-gated access devices, so there is no high-voltage wordline swing and no capacitive wordline-to-wordline coupling.
why: Constraint: removes ~3 V wordline CV^2 and pump loss and fetches only one segment, ~10x per useful bit; Fact 9: kills the wordline-coupling component of row hammer.

title: Double-sampling sense amps catch late-resolving bits at low voltage
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: Razor-style dual-sample sense with shadow latch | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Each sense amp latches at a nominal time and again ~1.5 ns later; a disagreement marks a slowly resolving low-signal bit, which is corrected from the shadow sample and its row queued for restore at higher voltage.
why: Constraint: removes the worst-case voltage guard band (VARY ~1 V to ~0.35 V, ~8x CV^2); errors are detected in situ without extra code bits.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO access gate removes the wordline pump
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: negative-capacitance FET with matched HZO gate layer | sense: standard | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: ALD]. A capacitance-matched ferroelectric layer gives the access transistor ~40 mV/decade subthreshold swing, so it reaches today's off-leakage at 0 V and today's on-current at ~1.1 V instead of a ~3 V pumped wordline, pushing the leakage tail down by orders of magnitude.
why: Constraint: wordline CV^2 ~7x lower and no ~3x pump loss, >10x on the wordline path; Fact 3: refresh drops with the tail.
